claims.text: Rare-earth-free, fully transition-metal NiFeCoCr-based high-entropy alloys can exhibit a magnetocaloric effect.
Controlled heat treatment can reduce the distribution of exchange energies in NiFeCoCr-based alloys.
Minor compositional tuning with an FCC-metal additive such as Pd can reduce the distribution of exchange energies.
Heat treatment or compositional tuning makes the alloy magnetically more homogeneous.
The untreated NiFeCoCr-based baseline has a wider distribution of exchange interactions than the treated or Pd-modified material.
The conventional baseline has microstructural or local chemical heterogeneity.
Improving chemical homogeneity decreases domain-wall pinning sites.
A narrow exchange-energy distribution produces a concentrated, nearly simultaneous reorientation of magnetic moments.
A narrow exchange-energy distribution permits small applied fields to trigger a rapid and reversible magnetic entropy change.
The proposed mechanism avoids excess magnetic hysteresis.
A robust single-phase structure preserves mechanical strength during magnetocaloric operation.
A robust single-phase structure preserves efficient thermal conductivity and rapid heat exchange.
Treatment that improves homogeneity will increase magnetic entropy change at low applied fields relative to the untreated baseline.
The treated alloy will have lower magnetic hysteresis than the untreated baseline.
The treated alloy will retain or improve its heat-exchange rate relative to the untreated baseline.
The treated alloy will retain or improve its mechanical properties relative to the untreated baseline.
NiFeCoCrPdx alloys exhibit a second-order magnetic transition with a composition-tunable critical temperature.
The hypothesis applies to single-phase, chemically disordered transition-metal high-entropy alloys near their magnetic critical temperature.
The mechanism may fail in alloys with substantial intermetallic segregation or excessive phase separation.
Failure of improved-homogeneity samples to increase low-field entropy change, or degradation of hysteresis, thermal performance, or mechanical performance, would falsify the hypothesis.
